message:
Let me look at the `xmlParseNCNameComplex` function more carefully. The issue is that when parsing a name, the parser reads characters using `CUR_CHAR(l)` and `NEXTL(l)`. The `xmlDictLookupHashed` is called with `(BASE_PTR + startPosition)` and `len`. 

The key question is: what happens when the name is at the very end of the input buffer? The `xmlDictHashName` function reads `data[i]` for `i < maxLen && data[i]` - if the buffer isn't null-terminated, it reads past the end.

But the README says the OOB read is "before the global table xmlIsPubidChar_tab". This is interesting - it means the string data being hashed is located in memory such that reading past its end goes into the `xmlIsPubidChar_tab` global array. This could happen if the string is stored in a static/global buffer adjacent to the table.

Let me look at how the parser input buffer is managed. Let me check `xmlParseNCNameComplex` again - it uses `BASE_PTR` and `CUR_PTR`. Let me look at how the input buffer is set up and whether there's a null terminator:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<｜｜DSML｜｜=command>cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul && grep -n "xmlParseNCNameComplex\|xmlDictLookupHashed" parser.c | head -20 && echo "===" && grep -n "xmlParserInputBuffer\|xmlBuf" parser.c | grep -i "end\|cur\|base" | head -30</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
